description: Founded by Ernest Garcia III, Ryan Keeton, and Ben Huston in 2012, Carvana set out to “change the way people buy cars.” The company operates an e-commerce platform for buying and selling used cars in the U.S. and, with its subsidiaries, offers related services including inspection and reconditioning, financing, and auction sites. Carvana debuted its distinctive car vending machine in Nashville in 2015, and now operates almost 40 of the glass towers showcasing its cars. Since launching in 2013, more than 4 million customers have chosen its automotive e-commerce experience to shop, sell, finance, and trade in vehicles entirely online.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: During the COVID pandemic, this used-car seller thrived as supply-chain problems made new cars hard to find; today business is booming as inflation makes new cars hard to afford. Carvana sold nearly 600,000 cars in 2025 at healthy profit margins, and its revenue rose 49%, helping it leap ahead 94 spots on the Fortune 500.

rankings.itemDescription: Breaking into the Fortune 500 for the first time this year is online used car retailer, Carvana. The company is known for its multi-story, coin-operated car vending machines, where consumers pick up vehicles after finalizing their purchase.
